description: Planned IT-STE rule concepts produced by reviewed adaptation decisions. These entries are not normative rules.

targets.working_title: Admit general vocabulary and domain terms
targets.design_intent: Define how general words and IT-specific nouns and verbs enter the controlled vocabulary through documented meanings, contexts, and terminology authority.
Make approval specific to meaning, part of speech, and form, including independent approval when one spelling functions as both an IT noun and verb.
Require one authoritative name for each concept within its context while preserving exact external names and documented mappings between interface layers.
Select the shortest unambiguous internationally understood term when no authority controls it, without prohibiting established or clearly defined IT terminology.

Use American English as the canonical prose baseline unless a governing contract, specification, style guide, or other mandatory external directive requires another variety; always preserve quotations, proper names, localized examples, and externally controlled or machine-significant literals.

Make an already selected multi-word term clear in prose without changing authoritative or machine-significant names. Show modifier relationships with grammatical phrasing, write a long term in full at first use in each independently consumable unit, and introduce an unambiguous contextual alias or abbreviation only when it improves readability. Preserve established hyphenation, add hyphens only when standard spelling or grammar requires them, and do not impose an absolute three-word limit.
